goal: Record `review_attributed` as a shadow, never-billed outcome on the terminal Lazy child run when a newly ingested review matches a sent Outreach row inside the 14-day Attribution window, and show the owner each Attributed review with its evidence on the Requests surface.
non_goals: Any Stripe, metering or billing change — `review_attributed` stays shadow / no-charge (map #617 decision 1, May §6.4).
Defining the billable-grade attribution precision bar (May §6.4 'M3') — that is its own effort and this ticket must not claim to clear it.
Lighting up the `already_reviewed` withhold reason — `batch-builder.ts` keeps `matchedReview: null`; a follow-up ticket owns the pre-send gate.
Backfilling attribution for reviews ingested before this ships — the lookback is forward-only from deploy.
Attribution on the Zernio backfill lane or the external-reply import lane — live ingest only.
SMS, WhatsApp or voice asks — email only, a destination constraint of map #617.
A new feature flag or env var — the write is inert by data and the owner surface gates on the existing `SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED`.
Solving the contact-to-review identity seam (spec D16d) — the match stays heuristic by design.
user_visible_behavior: The Requests surface shows a 'Reviews from your requests' section listing each Attributed review from the last 30 days.
Each listed review shows reviewer name, star rating, review date and the date the ask was sent.
The section states that the count is a shadow metric and is never billed.
The section shows an empty state when no review is attributed.
The section is absent when `SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED` is off.
A one-star Attributed review appears in the list exactly like a five-star one.
invariants: Tenant isolation: every attribution read and write is scoped by `account_id` and `business_id` (invariant #8).
Transactional outbox: the review INSERT and the `solicitation_attribution` outbox row commit in ONE transaction (invariant #2).
A matcher failure never fails review ingest — the match runs in its own worker, never inside the ingest transaction.
One review attributes to at most one Outreach row; one Outreach row attributes at most one review.
`unknown` delivery rows are never confirmed sends and never candidates (spec D12d).
Domain modules receive their DB client as an explicit parameter (invariant #15) — `attribution.ts` never imports the singleton.
No Stripe call, no `api_costs` row, no metered usage record.
Feature flags stay server-authoritative — no `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` companion (invariant #13).
The handler is idempotent on the deterministic outbox key.
Vercel stays UI-only (invariant #1) — the matcher runs on the Railway worker.
Review text and reviewer name never appear in a log line.
edge_cases: Two or more Outreach rows match the same review — attribute nothing, log `resolution: 'ambiguous'`.
The review carries a null or empty `reviewer_name` — no match.
The reviewer name is a bare first name with no surname token — no match.
The review anchor falls before `sent_at` — not a candidate.
The review anchor falls more than 14 days after `sent_at` — not a candidate.
The Outreach row carries `bounced_at` or `complained_at` — not a candidate.
The Outreach row carries `unsubscribed_at` — still a candidate; the person received the email.
The Outreach row already carries `attributed_review_id` — not a candidate for a second review.
The business has no eligible Outreach row in the window — the helper enqueues no outbox row at all.
The attributed review is later deleted — the FK sets `attributed_review_id` to NULL and the owner surface drops the row.
Names differ only by accents or letter case — they match after normalization.
The handler runs twice for the same review — exactly one attribution and one `review_attributed` outcome.
The matched Outreach row has a NULL `agent_run_id` — write the columns, skip the outcome, log it.

rollback_plan: Migration 114 is additive: four nullable columns on `solicitation_outreach`, one consistency CHECK, one partial unique index, one candidate-lookup index. Back-out order: (1) revert the code PR — this stops every enqueue and every write, and the columns go inert; (2) leave 114 applied, because inert nullable columns cost nothing and a DROP is the riskier act; (3) only for a full schema back-out, drop the two indexes then `ALTER TABLE solicitation_outreach DROP COLUMN attributed_review_id, DROP COLUMN attributed_at, DROP COLUMN attribution_score, DROP COLUMN attribution_detail`. No flag flip is required: with `SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED` off there are no sent Outreach rows, so the enqueue guard matches nothing and the surface returns null. Migration applies to staging Supabase first, then prod in lockstep at promotion.
observability: One structured worker log line per handled job carrying `resolution` from the closed set `attributed | no_candidates | no_match | ambiguous`, plus `reviewId`, `businessId` and `candidateCount`. Never the review text and never the reviewer name.
A rising `ambiguous` rate is the signal that the name rule is too loose — it is the direct input to the future M3 precision bar.
A flat-zero `attributed` rate after a staging send campaign is the signal the matcher never fires.
Handler failures raise a real Sentry issue on the terminal attempt through the existing `attachJobFailureSink`; no new alerting is added.
The owner-facing section on the Requests surface is the end-to-end proof — #633's staging campaign should render a non-zero list.
